title: Lesson 14: Spreadsheets and Data: Analysis, Cleaning, and Formulas
description: Grounded in Lesson 14 of the AI at Work series — cleaning data, writing formulas, and verifying numbers against the cells.

questions.question: Why does Lesson 14 say cleaning comes before analysis?
options: Because analysis is only as good as the table it runs on, and messy data produces confident wrong totals
Because cleaning is the only interesting part of spreadsheet work
Because the tool cannot read any messy data at all
Because cleaning is faster than analysis
questions.explanation: Lesson 14: garbage in, garbage out — except the garbage comes back looking polished. A messy sheet makes the tool silently skip text rows or count duplicates, producing a specific but wrong total.

questions.question: According to Lesson 14, roughly what share of a data project is spent cleaning and organizing data?
options: Roughly 80 percent of a data project is spent on cleaning and organizing data.
questions.explanation: Lesson 14 cites the commonly cited figure of roughly 80 percent of a data project spent on cleaning and organizing data, from a long-running survey of data scientists.

questions.question: What is the one habit that keeps all three spreadsheet tasks honest, per Lesson 14?
options: Check the tool's numbers against the cells in front of you
Trust the tool's summary because a number on screen is concrete
questions.explanation: Lesson 14: the one habit is checking the tool's numbers against the cells. Read the formula it gives you, run it, and hand-check a subset of the result before briefing anyone.
